description: Payload is the open-source, fullstack Next.js framework, giving you instant backend superpowers. Get a full TypeScript backend and admin panel instantly. Use Payload as a headless CMS or for building powerful applications.

sources.entry: Payload CMS - Developer-first headless CMS and application framework. (Source Code) MIT Nodejs

summary.one_liner: Payload is an open-source, Next.js-native headless CMS and TypeScript app framework that installs inside an existing /app folder and provides a backend plus admin panel.
summary.what_it_does: Payload provides a TypeScript backend with an auto-generated admin panel, usable as a headless CMS or as a framework for building applications. It can be installed directly into a Next.js /app folder, and React Server Components can query the database directly without REST or GraphQL. The README lists built-in features including auth, versions and drafts, localization, a block-based layout builder, a Lexical rich text editor, conditional field logic, granular access control, and document and field-level hooks. The admin UI and backend are described as extensible, and the README mentions a plugin system with official and community plugins. Starter templates for websites and ecommerce are referenced, with a create-payload-app CLI to scaffold projects.
use_cases: Headless CMS for a website or blog
Adding an admin panel to a Next.js app
Managing localized content with drafts and versions
Creating a custom backend with TypeScript types
Deploying a serverless CMS on Vercel or Cloudflare
notable: Installs natively inside an existing Next.js /app folder
Query the database directly from React Server Components
Official one-click deploy paths for Vercel (Neon, Vercel Blob) and Cloudflare (Workers, R2, D1)
Plugin ecosystem with official and community plugins
caveats: The README does not state database or platform requirements beyond the examples it names; the required-software list is referenced but not detailed
Some features and one-click deployments rely on specific third-party services (Neon, Vercel Blob, Cloudflare R2/D1)
Migrating from v2 requires following a separate 3.0 migration guide
